title: I build full games with no PC. Just my phone and an AI coding assistant. Here's what actually works
author: Unfair_Suspect_7425
selftext:
I don't own a computer. Every game I've made, the code, math, art, animation, sound and builds, was made from my phone, directing Claude running in cloud sessions.

The games are slot games (the casino kind, 18+). One of them is live and got the platform's top rating It earned 4 figures + in its release week. Here's what I learned doing it this way:

1. The AI writes code fast. The hard part is checking it.

Every game has a "prototype" version written separately, and the real engine has to match it exactly over thousands of test rounds. When they disagree, one of them is wrong. That one rule caught more bugs than anything else.

2. It can't see or hear, so give it something it can read.

For animation, every pose gets rendered to an image and checked against the original art. For sound, every effect gets turned into a spectrogram. That's how it caught a bug where every instrument was playing an octave too high, because the sample library labels middle C as "C3".

3. Art is still the bottleneck.

The math and code are maybe 30% of the work. Making a symbol feel alive when you win is the other 70%. I ended up building my own animation tool because static art kept getting rated low.

4. Small checks beat big reviews.

Before anything reaches me, it has to pass automated checks: no clipping, no clicks, loops with no seam, nothing cut off on small screens. I only judge what passed.

5. Phone-only forces good habits.

I can't "just open it locally and poke around". So everything has to be a page I can open on my phone: play the game, tap through every bonus, listen to every sound. That made my review process way stricter than when I had a PC.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow, the tooling or what broke along the way.
